newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips off highs but guard gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips off highs but guard gains.

text.p: U.S. blue chip shares came off session highs on Wednesday but remained positive and active in the wake of a Federal Reserve decision to leave short-term interest rates unchanged.
The Dow industrials were trading up around 12 points at 7317, below an intraday high of 7353, while Nasdaq rose over one percent to 1379, helped by strength in technology shares.
"We did better initially coming out of the block and we're seeing the market settle in a bit now," Ron Doran, director of institutional equity trading at C.L. King and Associates said.

While stocks were supported by yesterday's rate decision, with advancing issues outnumbering declining issues on the New York stock exchange by about six to four, the long bond softened following the release of U.S. trade data.

The benchmark 30-year Treasury was trading off 12/32 at a yield of 6.93 percent, following the release of data which showed the U.S. trade gap narrowed 13.9 percent in March to $8.51 billion, compared with a forecast $10.3 billion deficit.
The Nasdaq stock market, which was firm most of yesterday, received extra upwards impetus from shares of Dell Computer Corp, which posted strong first quarter results.
